full_text_en:
Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. v. Wenzhou Haihe Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. — dispute over confirmation of whether the technical solution falls within the scope of patent protection

【Ruling Gist】

I. When a generic drug applicant makes a declaration under Article 6 of the Implementation Measures for the Early Resolution Mechanism of Drug Patent Disputes (for Trial Implementation) that the technical solution of the generic drug it has applied for does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent for the reference listed drug, such declaration shall, in principle, be made against the claim of the reference listed drug that has the broadest scope of protection, so as to ensure the truthfulness and accuracy of the declaration. Where the China Listed Drug Patent Information Registration Platform publishes two or more independent claims corresponding to the reference listed drug, the generic drug applicant shall make a declaration against each of such two or more independent claims.

II. In a drug patent linkage litigation, when determining whether the technical solution of a generic drug falls within the scope of patent protection, the comparison and assessment shall, in principle, be conducted on the basis of the application documents submitted by the generic drug applicant; whether the technical solution actually implemented by the generic drug applicant is identical to the submitted application documents generally does not fall within the scope of review in a drug patent linkage litigation.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2022) Supreme People's Court IP Civil Final No. 905

Appellant (Plaintiff at first instance): Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Address: 5-1, Ukima 5-chome, Kita-ku, Tokyo, Japan.

Representative: Osamu Okuda, Chairman, President and CEO of the company.

Agent ad litem: Li Binxin, lawyer of Beijing Fenxun (Shanghai) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Shang Guangzhen, lawyer of Beijing Fenxun (Shanghai) Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Wenzhou Haihe Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Address: No. 360, Binhai 25th Road, Xinghai Street, Wenzhou Economic and Technological Development Zone, Wenzhou City, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal representative: Wang Renmin, Executive Director of the company.

Agent ad litem: He Yibo, lawyer of Beijing Yuntian Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Qiulin, lawyer of Beijing Yuntian Law Firm.

The appellant Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2021) Jing 73 Min Chu No. 1438 rendered by the Beijing Intellectual Property Court of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) on April 15, 2022, in the case of dispute over confirmation of whether the technical solution falls within the scope of patent protection with the appellee Wenzhou Haihe Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haihe Company). After the case was docketed on May 23, 2022, this Court formed a collegial panel according to law, and held a closed court session on July 5, 2022 due to the involvement of trade secrets. Agents ad litem of the appellant Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., Li Binxin and Shang Guangzhen, and agents ad litem of the appellee Haihe Company, He Yibo and Zhang Qiulin, appeared before the court. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The appellant Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. requests on appeal: to set aside the original judgment and render a judgment in favor of all its claims at first instance, including: 1. To confirm that the generic drug "Eldecalcitol Soft Capsules" (hereinafter referred to as the generic drug in question) applied for registration by Haihe Company falls within the scope of protection of the invention patent titled "ED-71 Preparation" with patent number 200580009877.6 (hereinafter referred to as the patent in question); 2. To criticize and educate Haihe Company for making an erroneous patent declaration and violating the provisions of Article 6 of the Implementation Measures for the Early Resolution Mechanism of Drug Patent Disputes (for Trial Implementation) (hereinafter referred to as the Drug Patent Dispute Implementation Measures). The facts and reasons are as follows: (1) The original judgment omitted the appellant's second claim at first instance, violating Article 155 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. First, Haihe Company only made a Class 4.2 declaration against original claim 2 of the patent in question, and made no declaration against other original claims (i.e., original claims 1 and 3-7) of the patent in question, and failed to correct the error even after clearly knowing that the relevant patent declaration was erroneous. Second, Haihe Company failed to notify the marketing authorization holder of the corresponding declaration and the basis thereof within the statutory time limit, violating Article 6 of the Drug Patent Dispute Implementation Measures. The above violations by Haihe Company clearly contravene the original intent and purpose of the early resolution mechanism for drug patent disputes and also violate the principle of good faith; therefore, Haihe Company's violations should be criticized and educated. (2) The original judgment's finding that Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. recognized that the application materials for the generic drug submitted by Haihe Company were consistent with the application materials for the generic drug in question obtained by the court of first instance from the National Medical Products Administration of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the National Medical Products Administration) constitutes a finding of unclear facts. First, Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. only recognized that Exhibits 1-5 submitted by Haihe Company were excerpts from the application materials for the generic drug in question submitted by Haihe Company to the National Medical Products Administration, but never recognized that the contents of the two were completely identical. The application materials for the generic drug in question obtained by the court of first instance from the National Medical Products Administration disclosed more information relevant to this case. Second, the evidentiary materials obtained by the court of first instance from the National Medical Products Administration show that the pharmaceutical excipient (antioxidant) used by Haihe Company in the prescription at the clinical trial application stage was dl-alpha-tocopherol, but the relevant content was covered in the evidence submitted by Haihe Company. The original judgment erroneously found that the contents of the two were identical and thus failed to ascertain the technical solution actually adopted by the generic drug in question. (3) The original judgment's finding based on the application materials for the generic drug in question submitted by Haihe Company that the pharmaceutical excipient used in the generic drug in question was A' constitutes error in fact-finding and application of law. First, the "technical solution related to the drug applied for registration" in Article 76 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law) refers to the prescription intended to be approved for registration as recorded in the drug registration application documents submitted to the National Medical Products Administration, rather than the specific substance selected by the enterprise for each raw material in the prescription. The registration application documents for Haihe Company's generic drug clearly record the use of pharmaceutical excipient A as an antioxidant in its prescription. The court of first instance erroneously compared the technical solution of selecting a specific raw material in the application documents, rather than the technical solution as recorded in the intended prescription for approval, with the amended claims of the patent in question, which constitutes an error in application of law. Moreover, according to legal provisions, the drug registration application documents should accurately reflect the drug technical solution actually used by the pharmaceutical enterprise. If there is an obvious contradiction or error in the description of the drug technical solution in the drug registration application documents, the technical solution actually used by the pharmaceutical enterprise for the drug it applied for registration should be ascertained, and it should be determined whether such technical solution falls within the scope of protection of the relevant patent. Second, in this case, the pharmaceutical excipient actually used in the prescription for the generic drug in question should be dl-alpha-tocopherol, or, in the alternative, the prescription includes two specific technical solutions: using A' and using dl-alpha-tocopherol as the antioxidant. First, the prescription for the generic drug in question uses pharmaceutical excipient A rather than A' as the antioxidant. Based on the information on pharmaceutical excipient A registered in the database of the National Medical Products Administration and the evidence of both parties, among the two substances A' and dl-alpha-tocopherol, only dl-alpha-tocopherol is the pharmaceutical excipient A legally registered as an antioxidant. In order to avoid infringement, Haihe Company intentionally replaced the pharmaceutical excipient dl-alpha-tocopherol with the raw material A' in the drug registration application documents it submitted, while the pharmaceutical excipient it actually used should be dl-alpha-tocopherol rather than A'. Second, the registration application documents for the generic drug in question show that the pharmaceutical excipient (antioxidant) used by Haihe Company in the clinical trial application process was dl-alpha-tocopherol. According to relevant regulations, the prescription applied for registration by Haihe Company should be consistent with the prescription used in the clinical phase. Third, in the Chinese pharmaceutical field, A is a general term for a class of compounds, including A' and dl-alpha-tocopherol. The prescription in Haihe Company's application for registration of the generic drug only specifies the use of A as an excipient, meaning that the technical solution includes two options: using A' and using dl-alpha-tocopherol. (4) The original judgment's conclusion that the donation doctrine should apply in this case is an error in application of law, leading to an error in fact-finding. First, the donation doctrine is designed to address whether a technical solution that is not recorded in the granted claims but is disclosed in the specification or drawings can be included within the scope of protection of the claims under the doctrine of equivalents. It has no application when the scope of protection of the claims changes during the subsequent patent confirmation phase. Second, original claim 1 of the patent in question includes A' as an antioxidant, indicating that the patentee claimed patent protection for the technical solution using A' as an antioxidant and did not donate it to the public. The donation doctrine has no room for application in this case. In the invalidation procedure for the patent in question, Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. amended the claims by abandoning the technical solutions in original claim 2 where the antioxidant was dibutylhydroxytoluene, butylated hydroxyanisole, and propyl gallate, but did not abandon the technical solution where the antioxidant was dl-alpha-tocopherol, nor did it abandon technical solutions equivalent to dl-alpha-tocopherol (including the technical solution using A'). Third, the evidence on record sufficiently proves that A' and dl-alpha-tocopherol in amended claim 1 constitute equivalent technical features.

Haihe Company argued in defense: All the claims of Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. are unfounded in fact and law, and requested the rejection of the appeal and the affirmation of the original judgment. The facts and reasons are: (1) The court of first instance did not omit any claim. The court of first instance determined during the trial that the appellant's second claim had no legal basis and could not stand as an independent claim. Furthermore, the defect in filling out the patent declaration was due to Haihe Company's insufficient understanding of the Drug Patent Dispute Implementation Measures. During the trial of this case, Haihe Company repeatedly wrote to the National Medical Products Administration and relevant units to request modification of the content of "Claim Number Registered" in the patent declaration. Moreover, within ten days after receiving the notice of response from the court of first instance, Haihe Company submitted relevant evidence and materials comparing the non-infringement to the patent to the court of first instance. Therefore, Haihe Company did not engage in any so-called bad faith conduct. (2) The original judgment found the facts clearly. First, Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. had acknowledged that the application materials for the generic drug submitted by Haihe Company were consistent with the application materials for the generic drug in question obtained by the court of first instance from the National Medical Products Administration. This fact is clear, and the original judgment's finding is accurate. Second, the evidence on record can prove that A' was used in the generic drug in question applied for registration by Haihe Company. It should be specifically noted that the materials related to the pharmaceutical excipient used by Haihe Company in the clinical trial application process are not evidence on record in this case, and are trade secrets of Haihe Company, not public information. Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., without any basis, fabricated the relevant "facts" and reached conclusions based on conjecture, which violates the principle of good faith. (3) The donation doctrine should apply in this case. First, the relevant judicial interpretation on the donation doctrine does not expressly limit the claims referred to therein to those in the granted patent text. Second, with reference to the adjudication rules established in prior cases, the donation doctrine applies to amended claims. Therefore, whether the pre-amendment claims included A' and whether Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. had the intention to donate do not affect the application of the donation doctrine in this case. The court of first instance correctly applied the law by using the amended claims as the basis for comparison. Third, based on the doctrine of prosecution history estoppel, A' and dl-alpha-tocopherol in amended claim 1 do not constitute equivalent features.

Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, which docketed the case on November 8, 2021. Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. requested a judgment: to confirm that the generic drug in question falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question. The facts and reasons are: Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. was founded in 1925 and is mainly engaged in research and development of biotechnology and antibody technologies and drug development. In 2014, Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. established Riken Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in China, which focuses on import, production, and sales, and is committed to introducing new products to the Chinese market. Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. is the patentee of the patent in question, with a filing date of February 7, 2005, and a grant date of December 8, 2010, and it is currently in force. Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. is the marketing authorization holder of the listed patented drug "Eldecalcitol Soft Capsules (dosage form: capsule; specification: 0.75 μg; approval number: National Drug Approval No. HJ20200058)". Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. has registered the above drug and patent on the China Listed Drug Patent Information Registration Platform (hereinafter referred to as the Registration Platform), and the above drug is related to claims 1-7 of the patent in question. On July 2, 2021, Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. amended the claims of the patent in question during the invalidation procedure before the China National Intellectual Property Administration (hereinafter referred to as CNIPA), adding "the antioxidant is selected from dl-alpha-tocopherol" from original claim 2 to claim 1, deleting original claim 2, and adjusting the numbers of the other claims accordingly. The amended claims include 6 claims. The generic drug applied for registration by Haihe Company is named "Eldecalcitol Soft Capsules", with dosage form capsule, specification 0.75 μg, and registration category 4. On August 16, 2021, Haihe Company identified on the Registration Platform that the drug it was copying was Chugai's "Eldecalcitol Soft Capsules (specification: 0.75 μg, approval number: National Drug Approval No. HJ20200058)", and made a Class 4.2 declaration, i.e., that the generic drug did not fall within the scope of protection of the relevant patent for the reference listed drug (i.e., the patented drug of Chugai) recorded on the Registration Platform. According to Articles 1 and 2 of the "Classification of Chemical Drugs for Registration and Requirements for Application Dossiers" issued by the National Medical Products Administration, the generic drug applied for registration by Haihe Company should have the same active ingredient, dosage form, specification, indication, route of administration, and dosage regimen as the reference listed drug, and must demonstrate consistency in quality and efficacy with the reference preparation. Therefore, the generic drug in question uses a technical solution that is identical or equivalent to the technical solutions of amended claims 1-6 of the patent in question, and falls within the scope of protection of claims 1-6 of the patent in question.

During the trial at first instance, Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. added the following claim: to criticize and educate Haihe Company for making an erroneous patent declaration and violating Article 6 of the Drug Patent Dispute Implementation Measures.

Haihe Company argued in defense at first instance: (1) The patent in question was declared invalid by CNIPA during the litigation period, and the invalidation decision is currently within the appeal period. Since this case is a dispute over confirmation of whether the technical solution falls within the scope of patent protection, and the conclusion of such determination will not change regardless of whether the patent is valid or not, the substantive trial of this case should proceed without dismissing Chugai's lawsuit, given that the generic drug in question does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in question. (2) The generic drug in question applied for registration by Haihe Company does not fall within the scope of protection of claim 1 of the patent in question. According to the relevant application materials submitted by Haihe Company to the drug review authority, the antioxidant used in the prescription of the generic drug in question is A, i.e., A', rather than dl-alpha-tocopherol in claim 1 of the patent in question. Furthermore, paragraph [0029] of the specification of the patent in question states: "The 'antioxidant' used in the present invention is preferably selected from the group consisting of tocopheryl acetate, dibutylhydroxytoluene, natural vitamin E, dl-alpha-tocopherol, d-alpha-tocopherol, mixed tocopherol concentrate, ascorbyl palmitate, L-ascorbyl stearate, butylated hydroxyanisole, and propyl gallate." Among them, A' is the antioxidant A in the prescription of the generic drug in question applied for registration by Haihe Company. It can be seen that A' is a technical solution described only in the specification but not recorded in amended claim 1. According to Article 5 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Disputes (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Infringement Dispute Interpretation), Chugai cannot include it within the scope of protection of the patent in question. Therefore, the generic drug in question does not fall within the scope of protection of claim 1 of the patent in question. Claims 2-6 of the patent in question are dependent claims directly or indirectly referring to claim 1. For the same reasons above, the generic drug in question does not fall within the scope of protection of claims 2-6 either. Accordingly, Haihe Company requested the court to reject all claims of Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in accordance with law.

The court of first instance found the following facts:

The filing date of the patent in question is February 7, 2005, the grant date is December 8, 2010, and the patentee is Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. At the time of filing the lawsuit, the patent in question was in force.

The listed drug of the patent in question is "Eldecalcitol Soft Capsules (dosage form: capsule; specification: 0.75 μg; approval number: National Drug Approval No. HJ20200058)", with the indication being osteoporosis. Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. has registered the above drug on the Registration Platform, and the marketing authorization holder is also Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. registered patent information on the Registration Platform for the patent in question. The registered information shows that the listed drug corresponds to claims 1-7 of the patent in question, the patent type is a pharmaceutical composition patent for a chemical drug containing an active ingredient, and the above registration information was published on July 13, 2021.

The Registration Platform shows that the National Medical Products Administration accepted Haihe Company's application for registration of the generic drug in question on August 16, 2021, with acceptance number CYHS2101591, and the reference listed drug (i.e., the original drug) is the listed drug of the patent in question. For the patent in question, Haihe Company made a Class 4.2 declaration on the Registration Platform, claiming that the generic drug in question does not fall within the scope of protection of claim 2 of the patent in question.

On December 30, 2021, CNIPA issued the Invalidation Request Examination Decision No. 53498 (hereinafter referred to as Decision No. 53498) in response to an invalidation request filed by a third party against the patent in question, declaring the entire patent invalid. This decision was still within the appeal period at the time the original judgment was rendered.

In the invalidation procedure, Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. amended the claims of the patent in question by adding "the antioxidant is selected from dl-alpha-tocopherol" from original claim 2 to claim 1, deleting original claim 2, and adjusting the numbers of the other claims accordingly. The amended claims are as follows:

"1. A preparation, comprising:
(1) (5Z,7E)-(1R,2R,3R)-2-(3-hydroxypropoxy)-9,10-secocholesta-5,7,10(19)-triene-1,3,25-triol;
(2) oil; and

(3) An antioxidant; the antioxidant is dl-α-tocopherol;

wherein the antioxidant is added to inhibit the degradation of (5Z,7E)-(1R,2R,3R)-2-(3-hydroxypropoxy)-9,10-secocholesta-5,7,10(19)-triene-1,3,25-triol into 6E-(1R,2R,3R)-2-(3-hydroxypropoxy)-9,10-secocholesta-5(10),6,8(9)-triene-1,3,25-triol and/or (5E,7E)-(1R,2R,3R)-2-(3-hydroxypropoxy)-9,10-secocholesta-5,7,10(19)-triene-1,3,25-triol, and wherein the amount of 6E-(1R,2R,3R)-2-(3-hydroxypropoxy)-9,10-secocholesta-5(10),6,8(9)-triene-1,3,25-triol and/or (5E,7E)-(1R,2R,3R)-2-(3-hydroxypropoxy)-9,10-secocholesta-5,7,10(19)-triene-1,3,25-triol generated after storage for 12 months at room temperature in the dark is 1% or less.

2. The formulation according to claim 1, wherein the formulation is a soft capsule, a hard capsule, or an oily liquid formulation.

3. The formulation according to claim 2, wherein the formulation is a soft capsule.

4. The formulation according to claim 1, wherein the formulation contains, by weight, 0.000001% to 0.01% by weight of (5Z,7E)-(1R,2R,3R)-2-(3-hydroxypropoxy)-9,10-secocholesta-5,7,10(19)-triene-1,3,25-triol relative to the oil, and 0.0001 to 12% by weight of the antioxidant relative to the oil.

5. The formulation according to claim 4, wherein the formulation is a soft capsule, a hard capsule, or an oily liquid formulation.

6. The formulation according to claim 5, wherein the formulation is a soft capsule.

Furthermore, regarding the selection of antioxidants, paragraph [0029] of the specification of the patent-in-suit states: "The antioxidant is preferably selected from one of tocopherol acetate, dibutylhydroxytoluene, natural vitamin E, dl-α-tocopherol, d-α-tocopherol, mixed concentrated tocopherols, ascorbyl palmitate, L-ascorbyl stearate, butylated hydroxyanisole, and propyl gallate; more preferably selected from one of dl-α-tocopherol, dibutylhydroxytoluene, butylated hydroxyanisole, and propyl gallate; and most preferably dl-α-tocopherol is selected."

To prove that the generic drug-in-suit did not fall within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit, Haihe Company submitted to the first instance court copies of the materials related to Excipient A from the marketing authorization application documents for the generic drug-in-suit. Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. acknowledged that the above evidence was consistent with the generic drug application materials for the drug-in-suit obtained by the first instance court ex officio from the National Medical Products Administration. Among the above evidence: Evidence 1 was the production prescription for the generic drug-in-suit, in which "Table 3.2.P.3-1 Batch Prescription" recorded that the function of Component A in the generic drug-in-suit was an antioxidant, and the implementation standard was ***. Evidence 2 was the excipient information in the prescription of the generic drug-in-suit, in which "Table 3.2.P.4-1 Source Information of Raw and Auxiliary Materials" recorded that the manufacturer of Excipient A was ***, the registration number was ***, and the implementation standard was ***. Evidence 3 was a supporting document for A, which was an attachment to Evidence 2, including the import drug registration certificate and import drug registration standard *** for A in the generic drug-in-suit. The import drug registration certificate recorded the drug name as A, the registration certificate number as ***, the dosage form as ***, and the manufacturer as ***. Evidence 16 was the registration and filing information of A in the generic drug-in-suit in the "Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient Registration Data" of the National Medical Products Administration, where the registration number of A was ***, the company name was ***, and the remarks were ***.

The first instance court held that: According to the provisions of Article 76 of the Patent Law, during the process of drug marketing review and approval, if a dispute arises between the applicant for a drug marketing authorization and the relevant patentee or interested party concerning the patent rights related to the drug applied for registration, the relevant parties may file a lawsuit with the people's court, requesting a judgment on whether the technical solution related to the drug applied for registration falls within the scope of protection of another person's drug patent. The drug regulatory authority of the State Council may, within the prescribed period, decide whether to suspend the approval of the relevant drug for marketing based on the effective judgment of the people's court. Although this provision stipulates that the relevant parties may file such a lawsuit based on the patent rights related to the drug applied for registration, it does not further specify the scope of the patents involved. Article 2 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Civil Cases of Patent Disputes Related to Drugs Applied for Registration" (hereinafter referred to as the Interpretation on Drug Patent Disputes) states: "The relevant patents referred to in Article 76 of the Patent Law mean patents to which the specific衔接 measures formulated by the relevant administrative department of the State Council on the resolution of patent disputes during the stages of drug marketing approval and drug marketing authorization application are applicable." The specific衔接 measures referred to in this Interpretation refer to the Implementation Measures for Drug Patent Disputes jointly formulated by the National Medical Products Administration and the China National Intellectual Property Administration. Article 5 of the Implementation Measures states: "Holders of chemical drug marketing authorizations may register patents for drug active ingredient compound patents, drug composition patents containing active ingredients, and medical use patents on the China Listed Drug Patent Information Registration Platform."

In this case, the patent-in-suit is a chemical drug composition patent containing an active ingredient, which falls under the type of patent specified in Article 5 of the Implementation Measures for Drug Patent Disputes and complies with the provisions of Article 2 of the Interpretation on Drug Patent Disputes.

Article 3 of the Interpretation on Drug Patent Disputes states: "If a patentee or an interested party files a lawsuit in accordance with Article 76 of the Patent Law, it shall submit the following materials in accordance with the provisions of Article 119(3) of the Civil Procedure Law: (1) Information on the relevant patents registered on the platform established by the relevant administrative department of the State Council in accordance with the衔接 measures, including the patent name, patent number, and relevant claims; (2) Information on the drug applied for registration published on the platform established by the relevant administrative department of the State Council in accordance with the衔接 measures, including the drug name, drug type, registration category, and the correspondence between the drug applied for registration and the listed drug involved; (3) The Class IV declaration made by the applicant for the drug marketing authorization in accordance with the衔接 measures and the basis for the declaration."

In this case, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. is the patentee of the patent-in-suit, and it has registered the relevant information on the registration platform for the patent-in-suit. Haihe Company's application for the generic drug-in-suit has been accepted, and the relevant information of the generic drug has been published on the registration platform. With respect to the patent-in-suit, Haihe Company made a Class 4.2 declaration on the registration platform, i.e., the generic drug-in-suit does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit. Based on this, in accordance with the aforementioned provisions, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. has the right to file a lawsuit on whether the generic drug-in-suit applied for registration by Haihe Company falls within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit.

It should be pointed out that although the patent-in-suit has been declared invalid by the China National Intellectual Property Administration, the invalidation decision is currently within the period for filing a lawsuit. In this case, both Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Haihe Company argued that a substantive trial should be conducted. Considering the above arguments and other relevant factors in this case, the court now makes a determination on whether the generic drug-in-suit falls within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit.

Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. claims that the generic drug-in-suit falls within the scope of protection of claims 1-6 as amended during the invalidation proceedings of the patent-in-suit, while Haihe Company argues that the antioxidant used in the generic drug-in-suit is A, i.e., A', rather than the dl-α-tocopherol in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, and therefore does not fall within the scope of protection of claims 1-6 of the patent-in-suit.

Based on the generic drug application materials submitted by Haihe Company, it can be seen that the excipient used in the generic drug-in-suit is A, which complies with the import drug registration standard ***. Comparing the structural formula of A recorded in this standard with the structural formula of dl-α-tocopherol in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, which has been confirmed by both parties, it can be seen that the two are not identical, and Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. also acknowledged this. Based on this, the generic drug-in-suit did not use the dl-α-tocopherol in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, and Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.'s claim that the generic drug-in-suit used the same technical solution as claim 1 of the patent-in-suit cannot be sustained.

Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. argues that even if the generic drug-in-suit did not use the same technical solution as claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, the two constitute equivalent technical solutions. Article 7 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Disputes" (hereinafter referred to as the Interpretation on Patent Infringement Disputes) states: "If the accused infringing technical solution contains technical features identical or equivalent to all the technical features described in the claims, the people's court shall determine that it falls within the scope of protection of the patent." Although this provision extends the scope of protection of the claims to equivalent situations, it is necessary to note that Article 5 of the same Interpretation also provides: "For technical solutions described only in the specification or drawings but not recorded in the claims, if the patentee seeks to include them within the scope of patent protection in a patent infringement dispute, the people's court shall not support it." This provision is a specific embodiment of the doctrine of dedication, with the purpose of protecting the reasonable expectations of the public based on the public notice effect of patent documents. According to this provision, for technical features described only in the specification or drawings but not included within the scope of protection of the claims, they cannot be included in the scope of protection of the claims based on the doctrine of equivalents.

Although the Interpretation on Patent Infringement Disputes applies to patent infringement cases, and this case is a case to confirm whether it falls within the scope of patent protection, the rules established in that Interpretation are equally applicable to this case. In this case, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. claims that A in the generic drug-in-suit is equivalent to the corresponding technical feature in the claims. Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. acknowledges that A used in the generic drug application materials is A', but argues that this technical feature is equivalent to dl-α-tocopherol in the patent-in-suit. Haihe Company contends that the technical solution using A' as an antioxidant has been dedicated.

From the facts found, it can be seen that with respect to A', paragraph [0029] of the specification of the patent-in-suit records the following: "The antioxidant used in the present invention is preferably selected from one of tocopherol acetate, dibutylhydroxytoluene, natural vitamin E, dl-α-tocopherol, d-α-tocopherol, mixed concentrated tocopherols, ascorbyl palmitate, L-ascorbyl stearate, butylated hydroxyanisole, and propyl gallate." Based on the above record, it can be seen that the technical solution of using A' as an antioxidant is recorded in the specification of the patent-in-suit, but this technical solution is not encompassed within the scope of claim 1 of the patent-in-suit (the antioxidant used in claim 1 is dl-α-tocopherol). Accordingly, in accordance with the doctrine of dedication embodied in the aforementioned provisions, A' used in the generic drug-in-suit and dl-α-tocopherol in the patent-in-suit do not constitute equivalent technical features.

Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. argues that the claim 1 before amendment encompassed the technical solution of using A' as an antioxidant, which indicates that the patentee did not dedicate the technical solution of using A' as an antioxidant. Therefore, the doctrine of dedication does not apply to this case. For this argument of Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. to be sustained, at least the following two conditions must be met: first, the claims referred to in the doctrine of dedication refer to the claims before amendment, or at least include the claims before amendment; second, the application of the doctrine of dedication requires that the patentee had the intention to dedicate.

Although a patentee may amend the claims during the patent validity confirmation proceedings, the amendment does not result in the coexistence or successive existence of two valid sets of claims for the patent; rather, the amended claims replace the pre-amendment claims, and the amended claims take effect retroactively from the beginning. This means that the claims referred to in Article 5 of the Interpretation on Patent Infringement Disputes can only refer to the amended claims. Furthermore, as previously stated, the doctrine of dedication protects the reasonable expectations of the public based on the public notice effect of patent documents, and it is unrelated to whether the patentee subjectively had the intention to dedicate. Therefore, even if the patentee had no such intention, it does not affect the application of the doctrine of dedication in this case. Thus, whether the claims before amendment included A' and whether Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. had the intention to dedicate are both immaterial to the application of the doctrine of dedication in this case. Accordingly, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.'s argument that the doctrine of dedication is not applicable to this case cannot be sustained and is not supported.

Based on the above analysis, although the scope of protection of claim 1 of the patent-in-suit may extend to equivalent technical solutions, specifically with respect to the technical feature of dl-α-tocopherol, the scope of equivalents does not include A' used in the generic drug-in-suit. Accordingly, the technical feature of using A' as an antioxidant in the generic drug-in-suit is not equivalent to the corresponding technical feature in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit.

Since A' used in the generic drug-in-suit is neither identical nor equivalent to the corresponding technical feature in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, the accused technical solution does not fall within the scope of protection of claim 1 of the patent-in-suit. Given that claims 2-6 are dependent claims of claim 1, and the technical solution of the generic drug-in-suit does not fall within the scope of protection of claim 1, even though Haihe Company acknowledged at trial that the generic drug-in-suit possesses the additional technical features of claims 2-6, it still does not fall within the scope of protection of claims 2-6. Accordingly, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.'s claim that the generic drug-in-suit falls within the scope of protection of claims 1-6 of the patent-in-suit cannot be sustained and is not supported.

In summary, the generic drug-in-suit applied for registration by Haihe Company does not fall within the scope of protection of claims 1-6 of the patent-in-suit of Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

The first instance court, in accordance with Article 76 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 2 and 3 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Civil Cases of Patent Disputes Related to Drugs Applied for Registration," and Articles 5 and 7 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Disputes," rendered the judgment: Dismiss the claims of Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. The case acceptance fee of RMB 750 shall be borne by Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

During the second instance of this case, neither party submitted new evidence, and both parties did not object to the first instance court's determination of the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the evidence.

Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. submitted two applications for investigation and evidence collection to this court. The first application requested the court to collect from Haihe Company the eldecalcitol soft capsules (specification: 0.75 μg/capsule) produced by it for drug clinical trials. The main reasons were: Based on the information on pharmaceutical excipient A registered in the database of the National Medical Products Administration and the evidence of both parties, among A' and dl-α-tocopherol, only dl-α-tocopherol is a pharmaceutical excipient A registered as an antioxidant. Therefore, there is reason to believe that Haihe Company intentionally replaced the pharmaceutical excipient dl-α-tocopherol with the active pharmaceutical ingredient A' in the drug registration application documents to avoid infringement, while the actual pharmaceutical excipient used should be dl-α-tocopherol. To apply for registration of the generic drug-in-suit, Haihe Company should have already conducted and completed drug clinical trials, so the eldecalcitol soft capsules produced by it for drug clinical trials can prove the actual technical solution used in the generic drug-in-suit applied for registration. The second application requested the court to obtain from the National Medical Products Administration the materials submitted by Haihe Company concerning the application documents for the generic drug eldecalcitol soft capsules (specification: 0.75 μg/capsule) involving excipient A, including but not limited to the drug instructions, sample inspection reports, supplementary applications and research materials for changing the type of pharmaceutical excipient, clinical trial plans, and study protocols indicated on the cover page of the generic drug application materials of Haihe Company obtained ex officio by the first instance court. The main reasons were: The evidence obtained ex officio by the first instance court from the National Medical Products Administration only involved the relevant evidentiary materials submitted by Haihe Company, showing that Haihe Company did not submit the application materials related to the excipient used in the generic drug-in-suit, and Haihe Company intentionally concealed the information on the pharmaceutical excipient relevant to this case in the evidentiary materials it submitted.

This court, upon trial, found that the facts found by the first instance court were basically true, and this court confirms them.

Decision No. 53498 was an examination decision made by the National Intellectual Property Administration in response to invalidation requests filed by third parties, Sichuan Guo Wei Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Guo Wei Company") and Chia Tai Tianqing Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Chia Tai Tianqing Company"), against the patent-in-suit. According to the decision, in response to the invalidation request filed by Guo Wei Company, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. submitted an amended version of the claims on July 2, 2021; in response to the invalidation request filed by Chia Tai Tianqing Company, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. submitted amended claims on August 6, 2021. The content of the claim amendments submitted on both occasions was identical. On September 23, 2021, the National Intellectual Property Administration conducted an oral hearing for the two invalidation requests. The examination text on which Decision No. 53498 was based consisted of amended claims 1 to 6 submitted by Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., together with the specification, drawings, and abstract as published in the patent grant.

In the submission materials filed by Haihe Company with the National Medical Products Administration under the project name "Product Development", it was recorded that: "***" In the submission materials filed by Haihe Company with the National Medical Products Administration under the project name "Control of Excipients", it was recorded that: "***" The drug name under the *** Imported Drug Registration Standard is "A", with the molecular formula ***.

The molecular formula and chemical structural formula of "A" (synthetic form) recorded in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia 2005 Edition Volume II and the Chinese Pharmacopoeia 2020 Edition Volume II are identical to those in the *** Imported Drug Registration Standard. The Clinical Medication Reference compiled by the Pharmacopoeia Commission of the Ministry of Health of the People's Republic of China records relevant information on "A (A')".

During the trial of the first instance, Haihe Company stated that on December 9, 2021, it applied to the National Medical Products Administration to amend its statement from targeting claim 2 to targeting claims 1-7, but the administration did not permit the amendment. Regarding the new litigation claim added by Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., the court of first instance explained that although a generic drug applicant should actively fulfill its obligations under the Implementation Measures for Drug Patent Disputes, the new litigation claim added by Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. was not appropriate as a separate claim and fell outside the scope of trial in this case, and therefore would not be reflected in the judgment. Both parties stated that they understood this.

During the trial of the second instance, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. stated that its amendment of the claims in the invalidation proceeding was to overcome the defect that the claims did not have sufficient support from the specification. Haihe Company stated that the generic drug involved was still under technical review and had not been transferred to administrative approval.

Opinion of the Court: This case is a dispute over the confirmation of whether the technical solution falls within the scope of protection of a pharmaceutical patent. Such disputes are a special type of dispute stipulated in Article 76 of the Patent Law. The core of the substantive trial is to confirm whether the accused technical solution falls within the scope of protection of the relevant pharmaceutical patent. This is not substantially different from the trial of the patent infringement determination part in patent infringement disputes, and therefore the relevant provisions of the Patent Law and judicial interpretations on patent infringement determination may apply.

In this case, although the patent-in-suit has been declared completely invalid by the National Intellectual Property Administration, both Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Haihe Company argued that this case should be substantively tried. Both parties expressed their willingness to resolve the patent dispute through this lawsuit before the generic drug involved is approved for marketing. Moreover, Haihe Company only defended on the ground that the generic drug involved and the patented technical solution are different. The stability of the patent-in-suit does not necessarily affect the trial of the disputed issues in this case. Therefore, this Court proceeds with a substantive trial of this case.

Based on the parties' allegations, the issues in dispute in the second instance of this case are: (1) Whether Haihe Company violated the provisions of the Implementation Measures for Drug Patent Disputes and how this should be handled; (2) Which antioxidant is the antioxidant excipient in the generic drug application that serves as the object of comparison in this case; (3) Whether the antioxidant excipient in the generic drug application and the dl-α-tocopherol in the patent-in-suit constitute equivalent technical features.

(1) Whether Haihe Company violated the provisions of the Implementation Measures for Drug Patent Disputes and how this should be handled

First, regarding the correspondence between the generic drug statement and the patent claims.

According to Article 6 of the Implementation Measures for Drug Patent Disputes, when a chemical generic drug applicant submits an application for marketing authorization, it should, against the patent information already disclosed on the registration platform, make a statement for each relevant pharmaceutical patent of the generic drug. The generic drug applicant is responsible for the truthfulness and accuracy of the relevant statement. This provision only requires that the statement made by the generic drug applicant target the patents, but does not specify which specific patent claims should be targeted by the statement. When making a statement, the generic drug applicant should generally consider the correspondence between the generic drug and the patent claims disclosed on the registration platform, that is, whether the generic drug implements the technical solutions of the patent claims disclosed on the registration platform. For a Category 4.2 statement, the core of such a statement is to declare that the technical solution of the generic drug applied for by the generic drug applicant does not fall within the scope of protection of the generic drug's patent. To ensure the truthfulness and accuracy of the statement, the generic drug applicant should, in principle, make a statement targeting the claim with the broadest scope of protection corresponding to the generic drug. Since the independent claim has the broadest scope of protection, if the generic drug corresponds to an independent claim, as long as the technical solution of the generic drug does not fall within the scope of protection of the independent claim, it necessarily does not fall within the scope of protection of the dependent claims. However, if the technical solution of the generic drug does not fall within the scope of protection of a dependent claim of the patent, it does not necessarily lead to the conclusion that it does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent. Therefore, for a Category 4.2 statement that the technical solution does not fall within the scope of protection, if the generic drug corresponds to an independent claim, the generic drug applicant should make a statement targeting the independent claim; when there are two or more independent claims corresponding to the generic drug with the broadest scope of protection, the generic drug applicant must make a statement targeting those two or more independent claims in order to ensure the truthfulness and accuracy of the statement.

After the patentee registers information on the registration platform, it is possible to amend the claims of the registered patent in an invalidation proceeding. However, regardless of how the claims are amended, the accepted examination text ultimately must not expand the scope of protection of the original claims. Therefore, as long as the generic drug applicant makes a Category 4.2 statement targeting the claim with the broadest scope of protection corresponding to the generic drug at the time of filing the generic drug application, any amendment of the claims by the patentee in the invalidation proceeding will not affect the truthfulness and accuracy of the statement.

The particularity of this case is that the generic drug applicant, Haihe Company, did not make a statement targeting the independent claim corresponding to the generic drug before amendment, but only made a statement targeting the pre-amendment dependent claim 2. In this regard, this Court is of the opinion that, in an invalidation proceeding, the patentee's amendment of the claims does not necessarily lead to a change in the examination text. The earliest point in time when the amended examination text is accepted and disclosed by the National Intellectual Property Administration is during the oral hearing process. When the National Medical Products Administration accepted Haihe Company's application for registration of the generic drug involved on August 16, 2021, the National Intellectual Property Administration had not yet conducted an oral hearing on the invalidation request for the patent-in-suit. Therefore, Haihe Company's application for marketing of the generic drug involved and its Category 4.2 statement came first, and the oral hearing by the National Intellectual Property Administration came later. At the time Haihe Company made the Category 4.2 statement, it did not make a statement targeting the independent claim with the broadest scope of protection corresponding to the generic drug at that time, but only made a statement targeting a dependent claim with a narrower scope of protection. There was no justifiable reason for this, and it suggests an attempt to avoid the main issue. Its conduct is hardly proper. Haihe Company stated that it had applied to the National Medical Products Administration to amend its statement, but this fact occurred after Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. filed this lawsuit, which makes it difficult to prove the justifiability of Haihe Company's conduct.

Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.'s method of amending the claims in the invalidation proceeding for the patent-in-suit was to merge part of the additional technical features from original claim 2 into claim 1, delete claim 2, and correspondingly adjust the numbering of the other claims. The scope of protection of original claim 2, which was the target of Haihe Company's Category 4.2 statement, is broader than the scope of protection of the amended independent claim. Therefore, the scope of protection of the claim targeted by Haihe Company's statement actually covers the scope of protection of the amended patent-in-suit. Considering that the Implementation Measures for Drug Patent Disputes are still in the pilot stage and only require the generic drug applicant to make a statement for each relevant pharmaceutical patent of the generic drug, and where the scope of protection of the claim targeted by the generic drug applicant's statement actually covers the scope of protection of the amended patent-in-suit, the people's court hearing a lawsuit filed against that statement based on the amended claims is consistent with the purpose of the early resolution mechanism for pharmaceutical patent disputes. Therefore, from a practical effect perspective, although Haihe Company's Category 4.2 statement was improper, it did not cause any adverse impact on the substantive or procedural rights of Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

Second, regarding the notification obligation of the generic drug applicant.

Article 6 of the Implementation Measures for Drug Patent Disputes also provides: "The generic drug applicant shall notify the marketing authorization holder of the corresponding statement and the basis for the statement. If the marketing authorization holder is not the patentee, the marketing authorization holder shall notify the patentee. Where the statement is that the technical solution does not fall within the scope of protection of the relevant patent, the basis for the statement shall include a comparison table of the technical solution of the generic drug and the relevant patent claims, as well as relevant technical materials. In addition to paper materials, the generic drug applicant shall also send the statement and the basis for the statement to the email address registered by the marketing authorization holder on the China Listed Drug Patent Information Registration Platform, and retain relevant records." This provision clarifies the notification obligation of the generic drug applicant. When making its statement, Haihe Company should have provided the relevant comparison table of claims and relevant technical materials. At the same time, when Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. registered the relevant information of the drug involved on the registration platform, it also registered its mailing address, contact person, contact information, etc. There was no obstacle for Haihe Company to notify Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. of the statement and its basis. However, Haihe Company only submitted the relevant materials after Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. filed this lawsuit, and did not provide sufficient and reasonable explanations. This does not comply with Article 6 of the Implementation Measures for Drug Patent Disputes, and its conduct is clearly improper.

In summary, Haihe Company did not make a statement targeting the claim with the broadest scope of protection of the generic drug patent, and did not timely notify the marketing authorization holder of the statement and its basis. Its conduct was indeed improper. This Court hereby specifically points this out and issues a criticism. Since criticism and education are not a form of civil liability, this Court does not uphold Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.'s litigation claim for criticism and education. Upon examination, both parties expressed opinions on this issue during the trial of first instance, and the court of first instance provided an explanation. Since this litigation claim was clearly untenable due to lack of legal basis, the court of first instance's failure to comment on it in the judgment does not constitute an omission of a litigation claim. Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.'s related appeal grounds lack basis and are not upheld by this Court.

(2) Which antioxidant is the antioxidant excipient in the generic drug application that serves as the object of comparison in this case

During the process of drug marketing review and approval, disputes between the marketing authorization applicant and the relevant patentee or interested party arising from patents related to the drug applied for registration are merely a special form of dispute over the relevant patent rights between the two parties. They are commonly referred to as pharmaceutical patent linkage disputes. For chemical generic drugs, the drug regulatory authority of the State Council conducts the marketing review and approval based on the submission materials of the generic drug applicant, and within the prescribed period, decides whether to suspend approval of the relevant drug based on effective judgments of the people's court on such disputes. Therefore, when determining whether the technical solution of the generic drug falls within the scope of patent protection, the comparison and evaluation should, in principle, be based on the submission materials of the generic drug applicant. If the technical solution actually implemented by the generic drug applicant is inconsistent with the submitted technical solution, it shall bear legal liability in accordance with the relevant laws and regulations on drug supervision and administration. If the patentee or interested party believes that the technical solution actually implemented by the generic drug applicant constitutes infringement, it may also file a separate lawsuit for patent infringement. Therefore, whether the technical solution actually implemented by the generic drug applicant is the same as the submitted materials generally does not fall within the scope of review in a lawsuit for confirmation of whether the technical solution falls within the scope of patent protection.

In this case, the evidence obtained by the court of first instance from the National Medical Products Administration shows that the production formula and excipient information of the generic drug involved, as submitted by Haihe Company, both record "A" as the antioxidant, which implements the *** Imported Drug Registration Standard. This standard corresponds to a drug named "A", with a molecular formula *** and a chemical structural formula as identified by the chemical structural formula in the findings of the original judgment. The information on excipient control records that the excipient adopts the corresponding variety quality standard in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia and the corresponding variety quality standard provided by the supplier. The molecular formula and chemical structural formula of "A" (synthetic form) recorded in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia are both the same as those in the *** Imported Drug Registration Standard. Authoritative publications refer to A as A'. The above evidence is sufficient to prove that the antioxidant in the generic drug technical solution submitted by Haihe Company to the National Medical Products Administration is A', not dl-α-tocopherol.

Regarding Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.'s claim that the antioxidant in the submission materials of the generic drug involved is not A', this Court is of the opinion that, first, the experiment content recorded in the submission materials is a comparative experiment using A and α-tocopherol as antioxidants respectively. Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.'s assertion that Haihe Company used dl-α-tocopherol as the pharmaceutical excipient (antioxidant) in the clinical submission process lacks basis. Second, the relevant records of this comparative experiment also indicate that the "A" submitted by Haihe Company as an antioxidant excipient is not a generic term for tocopherol substances, but a specific antioxidant listed alongside α-tocopherol. Third, whether Haihe Company's submission of A', registered as an active pharmaceutical ingredient, as an excipient for the generic drug involved complies with relevant regulations falls within the scope of review by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council, and does not affect this Court's confirmation of the truthfulness of the submission materials and the object of comparison in this case. Furthermore, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. has no other evidence to prove that the basis for the drug regulatory authority of the State Council's review and approval of the antioxidant in the generic drug involved has changed. Therefore, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.'s related appeal grounds lack basis and are not upheld by this Court.

Regarding the two applications for investigation and evidence collection filed by Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in the second instance, this Court is of the opinion that, according to Article 95 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, if the evidence that a party applies to investigate and collect is not related to the facts to be proven, is meaningless for proving the facts to be proven, or is otherwise unnecessary for investigation and collection, the people's court shall not permit it. As stated above, the basis for the technical solution of the generic drug involved should be the content reflected in the submission materials, not the technical solution actually implemented by the generic drug applicant. Moreover, the evidence already on file is sufficient to prove that the antioxidant excipient submitted for the generic drug involved is A'. There is no need to obtain other information from the submission materials from the National Medical Products Administration in this case. Therefore, this Court does not permit either of the two applications for investigation and evidence collection filed by Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

(3) Whether the antioxidant excipient in the generic drug application and the dl-α-tocopherol in the patent-in-suit constitute equivalent technical features

This Court has confirmed that the object of comparison in this case is the generic drug technical solution submitted by Haihe Company to the National Medical Products Administration, i.e., the technical solution using A' as the antioxidant. The A' in the generic drug technical solution involved and the dl-α-tocopherol in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit do not constitute identical technical features, and both parties do not dispute this. Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. argues that the two constitute equivalent technical features; Haihe Company argues that, based on either the dedication rule or the doctrine of prosecution history estoppel, the two should not be found to be equivalent technical features.

In this regard, this Court is of the opinion that both the dedication rule and the doctrine of prosecution history estoppel can constitute limitations on the application of the doctrine of equivalents. Their purpose is to achieve a reasonable balance between fairly protecting the interests of the patentee and safeguarding the public interest. If the conditions for limiting the application of the doctrine of equivalents are met, there is usually no need to further determine whether the two features are substantially the same in means, function, and effect, and whether a person of ordinary skill in the art could have conceived of them without creative efforts. In this case, since Haihe Company argues for the application of the doctrine of prosecution history estoppel based on Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.'s amendment of the claims, and argues for the application of the dedication rule based on the patent text resulting from the amendment, this Court first evaluates whether the doctrine of prosecution history estoppel should apply in this case based on the patentee's amendment of the claims.

According to Article 6 of the Interpretation on Patent Infringement Disputes, where a patent applicant or patentee, during the course of patent grant or invalidation proceedings, abandons a technical solution through amendment of the claims or specification or through statements of opinion, and subsequently seeks to recapture such abandoned technical solution within the scope of patent protection in a patent infringement dispute, the people's court shall not support such claim. Where the patentee amends the claims, if it asserts that a specific technical solution falling between the scope of protection of the original claims and that of the amended claims has not been abandoned, it shall provide evidence or give reasonable explanation thereof. In this case, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., during the invalidation proceedings, merged certain additional technical features from original claim 2 into claim 1, thereby limiting the antioxidant in claim 1 to dl-alpha-tocopherol, and deleted original claim 2, correspondingly adjusting the numbering and cross-references of the other claims. This amendment method essentially abandoned the technical solution of original claim 1, retaining only one of the parallel technical solutions from original claim 2, thereby changing the technical solution of the independent claim from being capable of using any antioxidant to protecting only the use of dl-alpha-tocopherol. Furthermore, the specification of the patent in suit enumerated multiple antioxidants, including dl-alpha-tocopherol and A'. A person of ordinary skill in the art, having regard to the content recorded in the specification of the patent in suit and the process of amending the claims of the patent in suit, would understand that Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., through amending the claims, made a clear choice regarding the specific technical solution for which it sought protection, and that it selected a single antioxidant from among the four parallel antioxidants recorded in original dependent claim 2, further indicating that its intent to abandon the technical solution using the specific antioxidant A' through the amendment was specific and clear. Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. neither gave a reasonable explanation for not including the technical solution using A' as an antioxidant in its amendment, nor asserted that the amendment was irrelevant to maintaining the validity of the patent right; in fact, it stated that the amendment was made to overcome the defect that the claims were not supported by the specification. Therefore, Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. has no reasonable grounds or evidence to prove that it did not abandon the technical solution using other antioxidants through amending the claims; accordingly, the doctrine of prosecution history estoppel shall apply in this case, and it is inappropriate to bring the technical solution using A' as an antioxidant within the equivalent scope of protection of the patent in suit.

In conclusion, the antioxidant A' used in the generic drug involved in this case does not constitute an equivalent technical feature with dl-alpha-tocopherol in claim 1 of the patent in suit, and the technical solution of the generic drug involved does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. Given that the above analysis is sufficient to reach this conclusion, this court will not elaborate on the other arguments of the parties concerning equivalent features.

To summarize, the appellate claims of Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. cannot stand and shall be dismissed. The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and shall be affirmed. In accordance with the provisions of Article 177, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court renders the following judgment:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 750 shall be borne by Zhongwai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
